clue.text: Browser and operating system — one to skip?

parts.note: Microsoft Windows is the best-known computer operating system
a hopper is one who hops or skips along

explanation.surface: Someone compares web browsers and operating systems, wondering which one to skip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Browser' looks like web software beside 'operating system', but it means someone idly looking in shop windows.
explanation.definitionFit: A browser in a shop is someone looking at goods with no intention of buying, exactly what a window-gazer does.

clue.text: I had Olympic Games organisers say, in the end, something daft

parts.note: I had contracts to I'd
the IOC is the International Olympic Committee, which runs the Games

indicators.note: in the end points to the final letter of the word say

explanation.surface: Someone recounts dealing with Olympic officials and calls the whole business daft.
explanation.walkthrough: I'D drops its apostrophe in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiocy is foolishness, and can name a single foolish act or thing.

clue.text: Kind sort of mother

definitions.meaning: kind as a noun means character or essential type, as in 'things of that kind'
Mother ... is the personification of the natural world

explanation.definitionFit: Nature means kind or character, and Mother Nature is a well-known figure, so it is a sort of mother.

clue.text: Cheers cricket team perhaps — one to be hailed?

parts.note: ta is British informal thanks, as is cheers
a cricket team is an eleven, XI in Roman numerals; football teams are elevens too, hence perhaps

explanation.surface: A cricket side is cheered and hailed by its fans.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is everyday British slang for thank you. 'Hailed' suggests acclaim, but a cab is hailed from the kerb.
explanation.definitionFit: A cab is something you flag down by waving from the street, which is what hailing a vehicle means.

clue.text: Waltzing Matilda — a place youre unlikely to hear it?

definitions.text: place youre unlikely to hear it?

indicators.note: waltzing has the letters dance about into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Waltzing Matilda, Australia's song, would hardly be sung in a far-off place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Waltzing Matilda' is a famous Australian folk song, so the phrase reads as a title rather than an anagram signal. Dalmatia is on the Croatian coast, a world away from Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: Dalmatia is a coastal region of Croatia, a spot geographically remote from the Australian song's homeland.

clue.text: Behold American private concern initially making sense

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold
a GI is an American enlisted soldier

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of the word concern

explanation.surface: An American soldier's private business is found to make sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Private concern' looks like a business, but 'private' is the soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Logic is reasoned sense, as in 'there is no sense in that' meaning no rational basis.

clue.text: Graduate female in family foundation

parts.note: a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate
sis, short for sister, is a female family member

explanation.surface: A female graduate in a family sets up a charitable foundation.
explanation.definitionFit: A basis is the groundwork on which something rests, the same as its foundation.

clue.text: Piping and what it may carry leading to difficulties

parts.note: piping hot means very hot
piping, as in pipes, may carry water

explanation.surface: Plumbing pipes and their contents cause a householder trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piping' reads as pipework, which is what carries water, but it supplies HOT, from piping hot.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in hot water is an idiom for being in trouble or facing difficulties.

clue.text: Big shot ricocheting, following a revolvers central line

indicators.note: following places the reversed shot after the letter from a
a ricocheting bullet bounces back, so the word for the shot is read backwards

parts.note: in cricket a six is a big hit clearing the boundary

explanation.surface: A big shot from a revolver ricochets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big shot' and 'revolver' suggest a gun; the shot is a cricket six, and 'ricocheting' turns it into XIS. 'Revolver' means anything that revolves.
explanation.definitionFit: An axis is the imaginary line through the centre about which a rotating body turns.

clue.text: Country serial broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast, in the sense of scattered widely, has the letters spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A country's serial drama goes out on air.
explanation.definitionFit: Israel is a nation in the Middle East, on the eastern Mediterranean coast.

clue.text: Pleasure craft exercises old boys back

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercises

indicators.note: back means the old boy pair is read from the end to the start

parts.note: read as boy's, a single boy is a lad, with the 's as a link

explanation.surface: Old boys of a school return to exercise in a pleasure boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedalo is a small pedal-powered boat hired out for fun at the seaside or on a lake.

clue.text: Holds regular newspaper feature for London landmark

parts.note: nelsons are wrestling holds, as in full nelson
a column is a regular piece by a writer in a newspaper

explanation.surface: A regular newspaper column covers a London landmark.
explanation.walkthrough: A nelson is a wrestling hold. The landmark is the monument in Trafalgar Square.
explanation.definitionFit: This tall monument to Admiral Nelson in Trafalgar Square is one of London's best-known sights.

clue.text: Home help turning up in a state

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: turning up, in a down clue, has the word for help read bottom to top

parts.note: aid means help

explanation.surface: A home help turns up in a state of agitation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a state' suggests being upset; 'in' is a link and 'a state' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: India is a sovereign nation, and a state can mean a country with its own government.

clue.text: Buzzing when wife escapes from flooding

indicators.note: escapes from means the wife letter leaves the word for flooding

parts.note: drowning can mean flooding, as in drowning the fields

explanation.surface: A wife escapes a flood amid buzzing insects or alarms.
explanation.definitionFit: Droning is a low continuous hum, the sound of buzzing bees or engines.

clue.text: Western railway twisted

explanation.surface: A Western railway line has a twisted track.
explanation.definitionFit: Wry means bent or distorted, as in a wry neck or a wry smile.

clue.text: What manager of pub must do presumably as part of a cycle

definitions.text: What manager of pub must do presumably
definitions.meaning: a pub manager has to deal with, or handle, the bar
the steering bar of a bicycle

explanation.definitionFit: The handlebar is the bar a cyclist grips to steer a bicycle, so it is part of the machine.

clue.text: First of two old PMs, perhaps, to produce bread?

parts.note: Pitt the Elder and Pitt the Younger were both 18th-century British prime ministers, so the surname covers two old PMs
A is first, as in an A grade or the first letter

explanation.surface: The first of two old prime ministers produces bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First of two' looks like a selection, but 'First' gives A, placed after PITT.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitta is a flat, slightly leavened bread from the eastern Mediterranean that opens into a pocket.

clue.text: Uses bug, maybe, or bugs?

definitions.meaning: to earwig is to eavesdrop, as one might with a hidden bug

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means to listen in secretly, and as a plural noun it names small pincered insects.

clue.text: Last month, Irish towns failed to complete sporting event

parts.note: Dec, December, is the last month of the year

indicators.note: failed to complete means the Irish town loses its final letter

parts.note: Athlone is a town in the Irish midlands; read towns as town's, the 's a link

explanation.surface: Irish towns failed to finish a sporting event last month.
explanation.definitionFit: A decathlon is an athletics contest of ten different events.

clue.text: Gander has beauty and elegance in the extreme!

parts.note: looks means good looks or beauty

indicators.note: in the extreme takes the two end letters of the word elegance

explanation.surface: A goose has both beauty and supreme elegance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gander' looks like the male goose, but it is slang for a look.
explanation.definitionFit: To take a gander is informal for taking a quick glance, the same idea as a quick peek.

clue.text: Disgrace being caught wearing light footwear

indicators.note: wearing means the caught letter is put on, inside the light footwear

parts.note: a sandal is a light open shoe
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone is disgraced when caught wearing sandals.
explanation.definitionFit: A scandal is an event causing public outrage and shame, a disgrace.

clue.text: Knocks loudly, bringing parcels

indicators.note: loudly points to the word for knocks as it is spoken

parts.note: raps are sharp knocks

explanation.surface: A courier knocks loudly when delivering parcels.
explanation.definitionFit: To parcel something up is to pack it in paper, i.e. to enclose it in a covering.

clue.text: Mails abused religion

indicators.note: abused means the letters are mistreated and knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Abusive mail is sent about a religion.
explanation.definitionFit: Islam is the monotheistic faith of Muslims, founded on the Koran.

clue.text: Snap the bottom off digging implement

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom is the last letter, which comes off the implement

parts.note: a pick is a tool for breaking and digging ground

explanation.surface: Someone snaps the end off a digging tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snap' reads as a verb to break, but it is the noun, a photo.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal words for a photograph.
